statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail risk remains in the low band: NQ futures made a fresh contract high at 31,094.75, failed there and retraced to 30,910.75 before recovering, which is two-sided price discovery rather than a no-retracement path. A narrow checkpoint window is flagged around the US cash open, the flash PMIs and the EIA crude report.
recommendation: Conditions remain consistent with normal mean-reverting behaviour outside a narrow checkpoint window of 13:30-14:45 UTC (15:30-16:45 Berlin), when the opening auction, the S&P Global flash PMIs and the EIA crude report cluster. Cross-asset signals are conflicting rather than aligned, which is treated as reduced directional conviction rather than as tail evidence. Existing-position management and emergency protection are unaffected by this assessment.
headline: Nasdaq-100 futures fail a fresh contract high and retrace inside a narrow 0.59% band; Tail held low with a flagged cash-open, flash-PMI and EIA window
body:
NQ futures are trading near 30,968, about 0.19% below the prior settle of 31,028.5, inside an overnight band of 30,910.75-31,094.75 that spans roughly 0.59%. The structure that matters for this assessment is the sequence: price posted a fresh contract and 52-week high at 31,094.75, failed to hold it, sold off about 184 points to 30,910.75, and has since recovered some 57 points. A failed breakout followed by a genuine retracement is the opposite of the pathological path this model scores, so Tail stays in the low band even though the index sits close to record levels.

Cross-asset evidence is calm but conflicting. VIX is 14.29, up 0.08 on the day, in a 14.12-14.38 range and close to the lower end of its recent distribution. The US 10-year yield is near 4.994%, up about 2.6bp and at the top of a roughly 1bp intraday range, with the 2-year at 4.76% on the latest H.15 release; that is a mild duration headwind for long-duration tech rather than a repricing. Crude has ended a five-session run of losses, with WTI near $90-91 and Brent near $99, after falling around 3% on Tuesday as Gulf flows improved and US-Iran diplomacy progressed. Delayed cross-sectional context shows semiconductors giving back part of an outsized prior-session rally, with all seven tracked names lower and a mean change of about -1.4%, while megacaps are split: Microsoft and Apple higher against Nvidia, Broadcom and Alphabet lower. Under the evidence rules, conflicting internals reduce directional conviction and lift Stress; they do not mechanically raise Tail.

The multi-day regime remains a bullish AI-led uptrend. The Nasdaq-100 cash index closed at 30,732.40 on 22 September, up 0.82% and at the top of its 52-week range, as Micron, Arm, Intel, AMD and Qualcomm rallied on continued enthusiasm for Meta's Muse AI assistant. That backdrop is why an alignment check matters, but alignment is currently absent: the chip complex is consolidating rather than extending, and the futures path is two-sided.

Three scheduled items cluster immediately ahead. The US cash open falls at 13:30 UTC, the S&P Global flash PMIs print at 13:45 UTC with manufacturing expected to ease from 53.9 to about 53.5 and services from 56.5 to about 56.0, and the EIA crude inventory report follows at 14:30 UTC. Neither the open nor the PMI print had occurred at the time of this assessment, so no post-event continuation is claimed. A 5-year note auction at 17:00 UTC and remarks from a Federal Reserve governor later in the session are secondary checkpoints; the governor's exact speaking time could not be verified and the event is therefore omitted from the calendar rather than guessed.

Looking further out, the Trump-Xi meeting in Washington on 24 September carries AI guard-rails and a tariff-truce extension on its agenda, with major technology chief executives expected to attend. It is a genuine source of unscheduled headline risk for the index, but its precise timing is not established and it sits largely beyond this forecast window, so it is carried as a conditional driver rather than a calendar entry. Consistent with the model's treatment of large scheduled surprises, an approaching event of this kind raises Stress and widens dispersion before it justifies any change in Tail.

lookbackSummary: All 24 preceding hourly slots carry a published Claude assessment, so coverage is continuous with no gap. Tail ranged from 10 to 21 and never left the low or watch bands. Three WATCH hours sit in the 22 September US session, at 14:00 UTC around the cash open and at 18:00-19:00 UTC in the afternoon, each resolving back into the low band within one to two hours. The trend-up labelling that ran from 18:00 UTC through 01:00 UTC reflected the record-high close and the chip-led rally; it gave way to normal through the Asian and European sessions as the overnight range compressed, and to mixed in the 12:00 UTC hour as internals split. Stress fell steadily from the mid-40s during US cash hours to the low 30s overnight before rebuilding into the European morning, and Confidence held between 84 and 88 throughout, consistent with continuously available futures price-path evidence.
outlookSummary: The forecast keeps Tail in the low band for 22 of 24 hours and concentrates conditional risk in one narrow window. Tail is 21 in the 13:00 UTC hour, which contains both the cash open and the flash PMIs, and 20 in the 14:00 UTC hour alongside the EIA crude report; those two slots are the only WATCH hours and both map to the yellow state. From 15:00 UTC the path eases back through the mid-teens as the session's scheduled catalysts clear, with a small step up at 19:00 UTC for power-hour flows and at 17:00 UTC for the 5-year auction. Overnight slots settle at 11-12 through the Asian session, the quiet-hours floor observed repeatedly in the lookback, then rebuild gently through the European morning. The final slot at 12:00 UTC on 24 September carries the highest overnight-forward reading at 18, reflecting the jobless claims release and the Washington summit day. Confidence declines monotonically from 86 to 54 across the window, which is the honest representation of evidence decay: current levels, ranges, yields, oil and the calendar are verified now, but none of the forecast hours' price paths has been observed. No forecast hour reaches the blocking threshold.

forecastDetail.comment: Cash open at 13:30 UTC and the S&P Global flash PMIs at 13:45 UTC fall inside this hour. Observed structure is two-sided: a failed push to 31,094.75 was followed by a real retracement to 30,910.75 and a partial recovery to about 30,968, so Tail sits in the watch band on event clustering rather than on trend evidence.

The EIA crude report at 14:30 UTC and any delayed second leg to the PMI print keep this hour inside the flagged window. Tail holds at the watch level; a retracement-free extension after a failed pullback would be the condition that argues for more, and it has not been observed.

Conditional step back into the low band once the open and the PMI print are digested and a first intraday range is established. Split internals limit conviction either way, so the mode is mixed rather than directional.

No scheduled US release in this hour. The midday liquidity trough typically widens ranges rather than removing retracements, which is consistent with conditional Tail near the low end of the recent distribution.

The 17:00 UTC 5-year note auction is the checkpoint. With 10Y already near 4.99%, a weak auction is the plausible route to a duration-driven impulse in long-duration tech; the score reflects that channel without pre-judging the result.

Post-auction digestion with nothing further scheduled before the close. Conditional Tail eases on the assumption that any yield move stabilises, with the day's extremes acting as the invalidation levels.
